name: metron
description: Local economic policy, accounting, autonomous customer email, and invoice document operations for AI agents.

interface.longDescription: Use four skills in one plugin: enforce economic limits and accounting, autonomously manage verified customer conversations through host email tools, generate private invoice PDFs from posted METRON records, and verify Circle payment settlement before reconciliation.
defaultPrompt: Use METRON policy, customer email, invoice documents, or payment verification operations.

review.commerce_description: METRON makes bounded direct Circle x402 USDC payments. A policy ALLOW automatically persists the Spend Intent as APPROVED and does not require separate human approval. ESCALATE requires explicit persisted human approval before it becomes APPROVED; DENY cannot execute or be human-overridden. Daily spend and available operating capital are absolute caps. Custom or legal commercial terms and below-minimum deals require separate persisted pre-acceptance human approval; customer acceptance always requires a distinct final human approval before invoice creation. METRON reconciles authoritative Circle evidence before accounting. EconomicRegistry V3 records independent typed facts and optional many-to-many attribution; revenue requires no spend. V3 awaits separate approved deployment and is disabled by default. The V2 Arc Testnet contract at 0x547552585d8d995c5063820b2950e0db52b4cab4 remains historical provenance. Circle remains payment authority and SQLite/journals remain business truth. Registry failure never reverses reconciled payment or accounting. The email skill may autonomously contact and reply to customers through connected host tools; those communications do not approve a deal or authorize an invoice or payment. For the Arc Testnet pilot, final deal and escalated spend decisions require a direct operator instruction in the interactive Codex chat, and scheduled runs never initiate approval commands. This instruction-based process is not production-grade authorization because the agent and operator share OS, CLI, and SQLite access. V3 deployment, activation and historical imports require separate operator approval; registry calls are provenance only. Status, service search, and estimate operations do not move funds. Testnet activity is not production settlement.
